opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for this role. Maximum allowable is write; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E040 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training max out at read; admin is never permitted for contractors. Recommend granting read.
reason: Jacob Ellison (E040) requested admin access to Source Code, but admin is not permitted: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, not Payroll Specialist (so even as a full-time employee, admin is not allowed). Additionally, the Security DB identifies E040 as a contractor with basic security training, and contractors never receive admin and max out at read without advanced training. Given the conflicting records, I grant the safest compliant level: read.
